From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@aurorahealth.io>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health — Ramp commitments & kickoff plan

Hi Marissa / Vivek,

Looping you in to formally hand off Aurora Health. Quick context up front: Aurora signed last week (SOW attached, signed via DocuSign), committed to a 6-week ramp with a target go-live for their pilot on 2027-08-15. Key SLAs they care about are 95th pct token latency <= 300ms, and audit log retention for 12 months.

What I’ve sent to the customer so far (attachments):
- Aurora_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan) — milestone dates and owners
- SOW_Aurora_v1.2.pdf — signed
- network_requirements_sheet.csv — baseline network & IP allowlist

Known risks / notes:
- They have a strict procurement timeline; Procurement (cc’d) may need a final paperwork item in the next 48h.
- They will evaluate quantized model variants during onboarding; expect a short quality check phase that could push GPU sizing.
- Data residency: US-only, but they will request a SOC2 evidence bundle in week 1.

Recommended next steps (please pick owners):
1) Kickoff meeting + roles — schedule this week (owner: Marissa suggested)
2) Infra readiness (VPC peering / allowlist) — owner Vivek
3) Eval pass (SLO baseline + quality checks) — owner Aditya for SE support
4) Procurement close / billing setup — I will stay on thread for visibility

Marissa — can you confirm who will be the CS Lead and whether we should schedule a joint tech deep-dive with Aditya this week? Elaine / Jonas from Aurora — please let us know any blackout dates for next 2 weeks.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Aurora_MAP_v1.xlsx, SOW_Aurora_v1.2.pdf, network_requirements_sheet.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health — Ramp commitments & kickoff plan

Thanks Tessa — congrats team, excited to run this. Quick answers and clarifying Qs: 

1) CS Lead: I will be the CS Lead for Aurora (Marissa Cole). I’ll own the kickoff and ongoing readiness.
2) Kickoff: I can host a 60-min kickoff this Thursday 07/08 at 10:00 PT if that works for the Aurora folks. If not, propose alternatives.
3) Tech deep-dive: Yes, please include Aditya for the initial SE session focused on model-selection and quality gates. Aditya — can you allocate 90 mins?
4) SOC2 / evidence: I’ll open a request with Security to gather the SOC2 bundle and standard evidence; Vivek, I’ll need your list of expected logs & retention config.

Clarifying Qs for the Aurora team (cc’d):
- Which environment will they route pilot traffic through (their dev VPC or a staging VPC we provision)?
- Any specific data classification tagging for requests?

From a timeline perspective I propose this plan:
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + procurement close
- Week 1: Infra readiness (allowlist, peering), initial SE run for model eval
- Week 2–3: Quality checks + small controlled traffic tests
- Week 4: Pilot go/no-go decision

Please confirm kickoff time and provide availability for the deep-dive.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

- CS Lead / Kickoff owner: Marissa Cole (owner)
- Infra & Networking owner: Vivek Kulkarni (owner)

- Aditya: Run a brief model-variant test with the Aurora sample prompts (I’ve attached their first-pass prompts in the MAP). Report SLO delta (latency vs. quality) by Wednesday.

Risks / mitigations (added):
- Risk: Procurement delay -> mitigation: AE to escalate to finance and offer a one-week provisional start with restricted usage while paperwork completes.
- Risk: Model quality regressions on quantized variants -> mitigation: schedule an extra SE checkpoints during Week 1 and reserve additional GPU capacity for short bursts.

I’ve uploaded the cleaned MAP and SOW to the shared Drive link (see related_links). Procurement, please confirm if you need any additional billing codes or an updated purchase order number.
